sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Caveman makes AI coding agents use fewer tokens. It makes the agent answer in short, structured sentences and compresses logs, test output and web pages before the model reads them, while leaving code and commands exact.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents spend many tokens on wordy replies and on reading long tool output, which costs money and fills the context window. Caveman trims both without changing your prompts or the code the agent writes.
whoFor: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode users
Developers who want lower agent costs
People hitting context limits in long sessions
Anyone who prefers short, direct agent answers
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if token use and verbose replies bother you and you want one install across many agents. The project's own savings numbers come from its benchmarks; your results will vary.
requirements: A supported coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and 30+ more)

overview: Caveman version 4 has six parts, all on after install and each with its own switch: Say less (short answers), Read less (shrinks logs, JSON, CSV and test output before the model reads them), Auto (picks model and effort per request), Blocks (keeps scripts the agent writes and reruns them), Waste fixes, and Browse (compressed web pages).

The caveman voice follows strict rules: answer first, one idea per sentence, never drop meaning words like not or only, and keep code, commands, paths and error messages character for character. Security warnings and irreversible actions still get full sentences.

Installation is one npx command that finds your agents and logins, shows what it will change and applies it. It runs on your machine with your own keys and subscriptions. Only Auto needs an account, which is free. The README cites outside evaluations by Adobe Research, JetBrains and Elastic.
